evidence: docs/plugin-helper.md prototype probe results; grep of plugins/*/src for std::fs, std::net, std::process finds nothing
result: recorded in docs/plugin-build/roadmap.md and docs/plugin-helper.md; to build with the deferred helper

decision: plugin UI: the wire contract (every new Widget, event, spec field and SDK builder for the programme) is written and compiled by the lead before any implementer starts; implementers write painters and hosts against it
why: aiongg's port method (contract stubs before writers) and LESSONS: a shared seam given to two parallel agents cost a redesign

decision: the framework painter lives on a second craft-libs branch, pluginkit-next = upstream next@bafb452 plus the three plugin crates copied from pluginkit by bin/sync-next; pluginkit stays on main
why: next is 2080 commits from main and lacks gpu, png and sqlite that EffectCraft needs, so pluginkit cannot move; a crate with its own workspace would need its own egui patch and lint config that next already has; when EffectCraft ports it pins pluginkit-next

decision: no painter trait: a painter is a function from a widget tree to UiEvents; painter-neutral conformance cases in craft_plugin_ui::conformance take a closure, and both painters run every case
why: one call site per painter; a trait would add a layer with one method

decision: status items, tool option bars and floating windows are panels with a PanelPlace (Side, Bottom, Float, Status, Bar), not new contribution kinds
why: one retained mechanism, one SDK shape, one test kit; the framework docks Float panels and may turn them into OS windows

decision: pen data goes on ToolEvent.pen only, not on the canvas Pointer
why: Pointer is built by literal in plugin tests (plugins/curves), so a new field there would break plugin source; ToolEvent gained a Default instead

decision: plugin panels opened by host::show_panel reach the dock through the existing window.pluginPanel frontend command (Event::Frontend), so automation and the plugin take one path; a Float panel is opened, then floated at its PanelSize
why: no engine change; the dock floats only open panels (found by the kittest)

decision: owner (2026-11-26): units run check and clippy only and test in the small craft-plugin and craft-plugin-ui crates; the lead builds and runs EffectCraft tests once per wave; no per-unit Sol review; each merged wave is pushed and the Plugin kit workflow runs
why: most wall time was linking the big EffectCraft test binaries in every worktree

decision: ui-lanes: overlay and tool replies while a panel call holds for 1 s went from 1.005 s to 0.36 ms sandboxed and 1.001 s to 0.14 ms native; a native command 1.001 s to 0.14 ms; a sandboxed command still waits (it shares the panel instance and its statics)
why: minimum of 3 runs, load 4.4-6.7, agent's test

decision: ui-pen: one unsafe module in EffectCraft, apps/effectcraft/src/mac_tablet.rs monitor, reads tablet pressure, tilt and eraser from AppKit; named in AGENTS.md This repository
why: winit reports no pen data on macOS and the egui fork is left untouched; AppKit event monitors have no safe binding; owner policy puts capability first; two SAFETY notes, one module
result: accepted by the lead, for the owner to confirm

decision: wave 2 from reports/ui-gaps.md: build 8 of its top 10 (drag undo grouping, command state, panel keys, eyedropper, right-click and double-click, panel menu and help, frame widget, list rename/reorder/sort); canvas zoom and pan and state across restarts are recipes, not API, because scroll and drag events and Root::Data already do them
why: the owner asked for everything UI needs, kept small; two items need no new API

decision: Contributions.ui_level (UI_LEVEL = 2): the SDK declares which event kinds it understands and the host sends newer ones (Context, Open) only to plugins at that level; drag undo grouping is host-only, not a UiEvent.held field
why: a new event kind sent to a plugin built last week would fail its whole call (serde rejects an unknown variant); UiEvent is built by literal in plugin tests

decision: conformance cases state painter-neutral claims: a radio is picked from the keyboard (Right then Space gives only the second option), a text area sends a last Text ending in a new line, and both painters name a tree twirl Expand <row> / Collapse <row> (the framework wording)
why: the three cases had asserted the egui painter's own behaviour; the framework moves focus with arrows and picks with Space, keeps typed text between frames, and names twirls Expand/Collapse

decision: ui-framework: craft-libs branch pluginkit-next = upstream next bafb452 plus the three plugin crates copied from pluginkit by bin/sync-next (never edited there) and craft-plugin-ui-framework
why: the framework exists only on next and EffectCraft needs main-only crates, so the painter and its test host live on a second branch that EffectCraft pins when it ports
result: a second run with the same sha makes no commit

decision: ui-framework: Grid::new takes its columns as Cow<'static, [ColumnWidth]> (builder level, reuse ladder step 3)
why: Widget::Grid's column count comes from the plug-in at run time; BodyLayout::grid already took a Cow, only the constructor narrowed it to a static table
result: every caller compiles unchanged (&[T; N], slices and Vec convert)

decision: ui-framework: new control craft_ui_widgets::controls::PaintArea, an area the caller paints that reports press, drag, release, hover and wheel samples (with pen samples) in its own space and every key as a chord while focused (KeyUse::RECORDER); one Default story; components-index row
why: Widget::Canvas needs an interactive custom-paint leaf; Picture::painter is display only and no other component gives pointer phases and keys to the caller (reuse ladder step 7, a library component in the lowest crate of its layer)
evidence: craft-libs pluginkit-next 6f79929d2; ui-widgets shared suite on PaintArea 6 passed; painter tests for a drag and a key
result: done; components-index.md row written by hand, the generator (gallery bin) was not run

decision: ui-framework: Fixture::catalog(AppCatalog) in the framework test kit
why: a trial can give run-time commands (a plug-in's) the way an app's FrameInput.commands does; the fixture had states and a gate but no catalog

decision: ui-framework: the conformance run of the framework painter uses the Linux key table
why: the framework maps the Menu key to a context menu only off macOS (behavior keys.rs), and CI runs Linux
result: 21 of 24 cases pass; three open conflicts in reports/ui-framework.md

decision: ui-framework-2: craft_ui::primitives::polygon_triangles, the ear clipping fill_polygon fills with, as indices into the caller's points
why: a plug-in canvas's concave polygon goes through the kit's Triangulate contract (craft_plugin_ui::filled_polygon with Host::triangulate); the framework already cut polygons but gave only a mesh, so the default triangulator reuses it instead of a second ear clipper

decision: ui-framework-2: PaintArea reports a secondary press as one Context sample, each sample's click count, and a hover only when the pointer reached a new place
why: UiEventKind::Context and Open come from canvases; the area reported a secondary press as a drag and a hover every pass, so the egui painter's exact event lists could not be matched
evidence: craft-libs pluginkit-next c17ff5b9f; trial paint_area::a_paint_area_reports_context_presses_click_counts_and_hovers_only_on_moves; conformance canvas right-click and double-click cases

decision: ui-framework-2: a row drag held in an edge band of rows that cannot scroll that way asks for no frame
why: edge_scroll requested a repaint in the band even at the top of a list or in a list that fits, so a held drag never settled (the reorder conformance case ran out of steps); a fix of an existing behaviour, not a new API
evidence: craft-libs pluginkit-next 7f084f0fc; trial list::a_row_dragged_into_an_edge_band_the_rows_cannot_scroll_toward_asks_for_no_frame; ui-widgets list trials 90 passed

decision: ui-framework-2: the framework painter's Host gives frames, triangulation, drags (a Drag to the Dropped its drop delivers), accepted files, a picture version, and the panel's keys and their presses
why: the egui painter's Host has the same hooks; one Dropped payload type makes the framework drag session carry a plug-in drag without a host payload type

decision: ui-framework-2: panel keys are framework key claims on every non-text control the painter draws; the panel menu and Help are command rows (DockPanels::panel_rows) whose commands join the AppCatalog; plug-in command state goes through CommandInput::state
why: claims are the framework's way for a focused component to take a chord before shortcuts; text fields keep their keys; dock panel menus run commands only
evidence: craft-plugin-ui-framework src/lib.rs, src/dock.rs; host tests the_panel_menu_shows…, a_panel_key_reaches…, a_command_the_plugin_disables…

decision: ui-fix-next: craft_ui::buttons::PictureButton, a button that shows only a picture fitted inside a rect of the size the caller gives, over a sunken well; Picture's image painting is shared with it
why: Widget::Image sends Click and has a size in points; Picture is a display component that takes no input and sizes by tokens, so the framework needed a clickable picture, not a painter workaround
evidence: craft-libs pluginkit-next 62bf8949a; suite PictureButton 6 cases; conformance case clicking an image with no upload yet

decision: ui-fix-next: the framework painter lays a plug-in grid's columns to their content, as the egui painter's egui::Grid does
why: fill columns under a vertical scroll squeezed every leaf (a 40-point image to 10.7, a button to 23.3), so a click at the centre the accessibility tree gave missed the image

decision: ui-fix-next: craft_ui::sections::KeyArea and Focus::take_presses: a press inside a stop that called take_presses which no control takes focus for (Release or Unclaimed) focuses that stop; the area takes its claimed chords while focused and is a Tab stop before its children
why: framework buttons release focus on a click (spec 8.3 kind 3), so after a click on Count nothing held focus and panel keys never arrived; a click in a panel focusing the panel is how Photoshop panels behave, and an opt-in stop keeps every other press as it was
evidence: craft-libs pluginkit-next f0febb760; trial a_click_on_a_button_in_a_key_area_focuses_the_area_and_its_key_arrives_while_a_field_keeps_its_own (fails with the rule off)

decision: ui-fix-next: the framework painter draws a panel that declares keys inside a KeyArea; the probe's counter panel takes Delete
why: PanelSpec.keys then reach the plug-in after a mouse click as well as while a control of the panel holds focus
evidence: craft-libs pk/libs-fix-next b7bdfad67, pluginkit-next e54bb876e; test a_panel_key_reaches_the_plugin_after_a_click_on_a_button_of_its_panel (fails with the rule off)
